rulebook.title: World Boxing Technical and Competition Rules (Olympic-style boxing, carried over from the AIBA rules)
rulebook.text_used: written from general knowledge of the AIBA / World Boxing technical and competition rules; the federation sites were not reachable from this session, so rule wording, glove weights and ring sizes were not re-checked. Professional bodies (WBC, WBA, IBF, WBO) differ in details (ring size, gloves, headguards).

ring_m.note: Olympic-style rule; professional rings are 4.9-7.3 m inside the ropes

gloves_oz.note: AIBA-era split; check the event's current rule

scene.text: Square ring with four ropes, one red corner, one blue corner and two white neutral corners; the canvas covers a padded floor.
Each boxer wears the colour of the corner (red or blue) on the vest, shorts, gloves and headguard; the waistband of the shorts marks the belt line and must be clearly visible.
Mouthguard in every bout; hand wraps under the gloves; groin guard; elite men usually box without headguards (women, youth and juniors often wear them, check the event).
One referee inside the ring; judges seated at ringside; each boxer has a coach in the corner.

fouls.title: Hitting below the belt
fouls.text: Blows must land on the front or sides of the head or body above the belt line; hitting below the belt is a foul.
fouls.legal: both gloves stay above the opponent's belt line

fouls.title: Knuckle part of the closed glove
fouls.text: A scoring blow lands with the knuckle part of the closed glove; hitting with the open glove, the inside of the glove, the wrist or the side of the hand is a foul.
fouls.legal: both hands are closed fists inside the gloves

fouls.title: Head butts and elbows
fouls.text: Butting, or attacking with the head, shoulder, forearm or elbow, is a foul; only the fist in the glove may strike.

fouls.rule: Fouls: back of the head, neck, kidneys
fouls.title: Rabbit punch and kidney punch
fouls.text: Blows to the back of the head or neck and to the kidneys are fouls; the target is the front and sides of the head and body.
avoid: punch to the back of the head

fouls.title: Holding and wrestling
fouls.text: Holding, hooking the opponent's arm or neck, pushing, tripping, wrestling or throwing is a foul, and so is holding and hitting at the same time.
avoid: arm locked around the opponent's neck

fouls.title: Ducking below the belt
fouls.text: Ducking so low that the head goes below the opponent's belt line is a foul.
avoid: boxer ducking with the head at waist height
